lessons.pregame_expectation: Nebraska holds the largest measured edge in this matchup: Nebraska 62.9 (#15 of 138) vs Oregon 44.3 (#100 of 138) — 85 places on the national board.
lessons.actual_result: Nebraska Cornhuskers 2.36 yards per carry against Oregon Ducks 3.4; Nebraska Cornhuskers 78 rushing yards against Oregon Ducks 129.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Nebraska as better in rushing and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 21.3 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 9 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.actual_result: It graded a win. The reasoning behind it did not hold: 1 of 1 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
lessons.lesson: A winning number built on a reading the game contradicted. Nothing about this result should increase confidence in the mechanism EdgeDesk named, and treating it as confirmation is how a model gets worse while its record gets better.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Why did the number land while the mechanism failed? Either the number was right for a reason EdgeDesk has not identified, or it was luck. Both are worth knowing and they are different.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 54.5.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 31 points, an error of 23.5.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Oregon −0.5 where the market has Oregon −12.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings — a 11.8 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Oregon Ducks won by 3. the result landed on EdgeDesk’s side of the market number: Oregon Ducks beat a margin of -12.5
lessons.lesson: The disagreement landed. One landing proves nothing on its own; the aggregate of them, held against the closing line, is the only thing that would.
